title: kv-cache: fragmentation-aware eviction, smarter spillover paging, and defrag scheduler
author: Maya Chen
description: Context: KV cache memory churn, fragmentation, and suboptimal spill decisions have caused increased OOM risk and degraded tail latency on long-response workloads. This PR implements three complementary improvements: 1) a fragmentation-aware eviction policy that factors contiguous span size and fragmentation score into eviction heuristics, 2) a spillover paging subsystem that pages cold KV segments to host memory/SSD in large contiguous pages to avoid excessive pointer-chasing, and 3) a low-impact defragmentation scheduler that compacts hot shards during low load windows. Motivation: prior strategies evicted by simple LRU or per-key weight which often left behind many small fragments, increasing memory overhead and preventing efficient paging. This leads to increased GC-like work and worse end-to-end latency for long-context generation. What changed: - eviction_policy.rs: added FragmentationScore and integrated it into the priority calculation (recency, frequency, size, frag_score). - spillover_pager.rs: new module implementing page-aligned spill/restore paths with async prefetch for predicted prefixes. - defrag_scheduler.rs: background worker that coalesces adjacent free ranges and relocates small fragments when the shard's fragmentation score exceeds a threshold. - runtime/kv_cache: added locking refinements to minimize contention during defrag and spill operations; introduced a lockless fast-path for common reads. - metrics: new metrics for kv_fragmentation_score, spill_pages_written, spill_pages_read, defrag_runs, defrag_moved_bytes. - config: new knobs added to per-customer config (spill_page_size, defrag_threshold, defrag_max_io_bytes). Tests & benchmarks: unit tests covering eviction ranking, integration tests for async spill/restore, and a perf canary showing median latency unchanged and 95th improving by ~12% on long-context (32k) workloads. Rollout plan: feature gated behind kv.cache.experimental=true; default disabled for private installs until opted in. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (ENG-1984) - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests - [x] Perf canary - [x] Docs update (runtime/kv_cache/README) - [x] Feature flag gating - [x] Add observability metrics Notes: this description contains a single continuous string including the checklist above and references to the changed modules.

review_comments: Arjun Patel (2025-11-22): Overall looks solid. A few concerns: (1) defrag relocations could interfere with continuous batching - have you measured impact on in-flight requests? (2) spill page size default 64KB seems conservative; can we justify?

Maya Chen (2025-11-23): Reply: for (1) defrag runs are scheduled only when shard_load < defrag_load_threshold and relocate ops use async handoff; added microbench that shows negligible impact on steady-state throughput (included in bench commit). For (2) 64KB chosen empirically to balance IO amplification vs. read amplification; added config knob and note in README.
Lina Ortega (2025-11-25): Please add more exhaustive tests around eviction ordering when frag_score and recency compete. Also add a comment about linearizability guarantees during move operations.
Maya Chen (2025-11-27): Added tests and comments; tightened move protocol to publish a tombstone before relocating to preserve read-path correctness. PTAL.
Noah Kim (2025-11-29): Perf canary failed on first run due to a race in the pager write path (flaky test). Identified missing ordering on async flush; request a fix and rerun.
Maya Chen (2025-11-30): Fixed ordering by awaiting the writer future in the pager flush path and added deterministic test; reran perf canary (green).
Arjun Patel (2025-12-02): Approved after addressing comments. Lina approved as well.
merge_commit_message:
kv-cache: fragmentation-aware eviction + spillover pager + defrag scheduler (ENG-1984)

Improves memory utilization and tail latency by compacting fragments and paging cold segments as large pages.
release_notes: kv-cache: improved eviction policy reduces fragmentation and OOMs; configurable defrag scheduler and spillover pager (opt-in behind kv.cache.experimental)
Observability: new fragmentation and spill metrics available (kv_fragmentation_score, spill_pages_written, defrag_runs)
Performance: 95th latency improved ~12% for long-context workloads in our canary
